mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and consumer price index signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and rising inflation, compressing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (FEDFUNDS * CPIAUCSL) shows no significant negative correlation with 20-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (UNRATE below 5.0% and declining for 3 months), a rising unemployment rate signals economic overheating and impending policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, 60-day SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises by more than 0.1 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: HOUST growth rate shows no positive correlation with 20-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales growth exceeds 0.5% month-over-month, it signals robust consumer spending that boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when RSAFS growth exceeds 0.5% m/m.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and non-farm payrolls signals a broad-based economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (INDPRO * PAYEMS) shows no significant negative correlation with 20-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that may lead to wage inflation and monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0%.
